terms.definition: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons and different masses.
terms.examiner: Same number of protons and electrons, different number of neutrons. "Different mass numbers" alone is not enough when the question asks about atomic structure.

terms.definition: The mass of an isotope compared with 1/12th of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
terms.examiner: The comparison with 1/12th of carbon-12 is the mark; "compared with carbon-12" without the twelfth loses it.

terms.definition: The weighted mean mass of an atom of an element compared with 1/12th of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
terms.examiner: Three ideas are credited: weighted mean, of an atom, compared with 1/12th of carbon-12. "Average" without "weighted" is commonly penalised.

terms.definition: The weighted mean mass of a molecule compared with 1/12th of the mass of an atom of carbon-12. Relative formula mass is used for giant structures.
terms.examiner: Use "relative formula mass" for ionic compounds, which have no molecules.

terms.definition: The number of protons plus neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.
terms.examiner: Atomic number is the number of protons only; it identifies the element.

terms.definition: An atom or group of atoms with a charge, formed by the loss or gain of electrons.
terms.examiner: For a positive ion, electrons = protons − charge; for a negative ion, electrons = protons + charge.
